lines.en: Morning, Amara! You're up early. I've been awake since five because my shift at the bakery starts at six.
lines.pt: Bom dia, Amara! Você acordou cedo. Estou de pé desde as cinco porque meu turno na padaria começa às seis.

lines.en: I couldn't sleep, honestly. It's so humid here that I kept waking up, and I'm not used to waking up that early.
lines.pt: Não consegui dormir, sinceramente. Aqui é tão úmido que eu acordei várias vezes, e não estou acostumada a acordar tão cedo.

lines.en: Give it a week. When I first moved here from Melbourne, the humidity felt exhausting.
lines.pt: Dê uma semana. Quando me mudei de Melbourne, a umidade parecia exaustiva.

lines.en: In my old apartment I lived alone, so sharing one bathroom with four flatmates will take some adjusting.
lines.pt: No meu antigo apartamento eu morava sozinha, então dividir um banheiro com quatro colegas de casa vai exigir uma adaptação.

lines.en: We keep a roster on the fridge. Everybody cooks once a week, and on Fridays we just order takeaway from the Thai place downstairs.
lines.pt: A gente deixa uma escala na geladeira. Todo mundo cozinha uma vez por semana, e nas sextas pedimos comida do restaurante tailandês aqui embaixo.

lines.en: That's a relief, because I can't cook much. Wait, do you really work a shift that starts at six every single day?
lines.pt: Que alívio, porque eu cozinho muito mal. Espera, você realmente trabalha num turno que começa às seis todo santo dia?

lines.en: Five days a week, yes. Honestly, after three years I'm used to getting up before the sun.
lines.pt: Cinco dias por semana, sim. Sinceramente, depois de três anos já estou acostumado a levantar antes do sol.

lines.en: Three years! I'd go crazy. I worked evenings at a call center once, and sleeping until nine was the only thing that kept me sane.
lines.pt: Três anos! Eu enlouqueceria. Já trabalhei à noite num call center, e dormir até as nove era a única coisa que me mantinha sã.

lines.en: Ha, we're opposites then. Are you used to the heat yet, or are you planning to hide in the air conditioning all weekend?
lines.pt: Ha, somos opostos, então. Já se acostumou com o calor, ou vai se esconder no ar-condicionado o fim de semana todo?

lines.en: Not yet! But the Expo 88 exhibit at the museum sounds interesting, and it's indoors. Do you want to come with me on Saturday?
lines.pt: Ainda não! Mas a exposição sobre a Expo 88 no museu parece interessante, e é em local fechado. Quer ir comigo no sábado?

lines.en: Sure, as long as we get there before the crowds. I'll even set my alarm for eight, just this once.
lines.pt: Claro, desde que a gente chegue antes da multidão. Até vou programar o despertador para as oito, só desta vez.

facts.label: Be used to
facts.sub: Já é normal: I’m used to getting up early. Negativa: I’m not used to cooking. Pergunta: Are you used to it? Não confunda com I used to + infinitivo.

facts.label: Estar acostumado
facts.sub: Use be used to + -ing para algo que já é normal para você: I’m used to getting up early. Forma: be + used to + verbo com -ing. Em português: “estou acostumado a acordar cedo”.

facts.label: Not used to
facts.sub: Para negar: I’m not used to waking up early. Para perguntar: Are you used to the heat yet? Use o verbo be (am, is, are, was, were) e não do/does.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Be used to + -ing describes something that is normal for you.
After “used to” in this meaning we use the infinitive.
items.why: We use the -ing form: I’m used to getting up early.

items.s: “I’m not used to cooking” means cooking is not familiar.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Be used to + -ing describes something that is normal for you. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
After “used to” in this meaning we use the infinitive. → Falso (We use the -ing form: I’m used to getting up early.)
“I’m not used to cooking” means cooking is not familiar. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A new routine in Brisbane · 1/3
paragraphs: It is five in the morning in a quiet house in Brisbane. Fern is already awake and cooking breakfast. Her friend Leo has just moved in for the summer. He is tired and not used to the early sun. The fridge has a list of chores. They talk about their habits.

“Leo, I’m used to getting up at five, so I’m always the first person awake in this house.” says Fern. “I’m not used to waking up that early. I’m used to staying up late and sleeping until nine.” says Leo. “I worked night shifts for years, so I’m used to eating dinner at midnight.” says Fern.

pages.title: A new routine in Brisbane · 2/3
paragraphs: “That sounds exhausting. I’m not used to working under pressure, and I’m not used to being alone in a big house.” says Leo. “You’re not used to cooking either, are you? I’m used to making breakfast for everyone before they wake up.” says Fern. “Honestly, I’m used to ordering takeaway. Mum cooked well, but I’m not used to doing the dishes afterwards.” says Leo.

“In this house we’re all used to sharing the chores, so you’ll have to learn. It isn’t hard.” says Fern. “I know. My flatmates in Melbourne weren’t used to cleaning either, and the kitchen was a disaster.” says Leo. “Ha! Are you used to the heat yet? Brisbane summers are humid, and visitors aren’t used to sweating so much.” says Fern.
